posts.t: Si tú quieres ir de aquí a Italia y te cuesta 100 euros el vuelo, coge un vuelo de aquí a Alemania
posts.c:
Si decides arriesgarte haciendo esto, cosa que no aconsejo... aquí tienes lo que hay que saber antes de bajarte en la escala:
La web: skiplagged.com

✈️ Solo equipaje de mano. La maleta facturada sigue hasta el destino del billete, no hasta el tuyo. En el propio buscador lo avisan: "sólo mochila".

🎫 Solo billetes de ida. Si lo haces en la ida de un ida y vuelta, la aerolínea te cancela la vuelta en cuanto no embarcas en el segundo tramo.

🪪 Sin número de viajero frecuente. Es el hilo del que tiran para identificarte. Cuenta nueva o sin cuenta.

🔁 No lo repitas con la misma compañía. Persiguen patrones, y varias ya lo detectan con sistemas automáticos.

🛂 Ojo si tu destino "oficial" está fuera de la UE y tu escala dentro: el control de fronteras espera que sigas viaje, y ahí la cosa se complica.

⚖️ No es ilegal, pero rompe las condiciones del contrato de transporte. Pueden anularte vuelos, reclamarte la diferencia o vetarte. Tú decides si el ahorro compensa.

Y el matiz que casi nadie cuenta: esto rinde en Estados Unidos, donde los vuelos pasan por hubs. En Europa volamos punto a punto con decenas de low cost, así que el directo suele ganar. Compruébalo antes de montarte la película.

posts.t: Most people build only Machine Learning Projects or Only Quant Projects,but when you combine the
posts.c:
Most people build only Machine Learning Projects or Only Quant Projects,but when you combine the fields you stand out way more than the other applicants as it shows you can build the algorithms that run the industry

1. Stock Price Regime Detector – classify market conditions (trending, mean-reverting, volatile) using Hidden Markov Models or clustering, then adapt strategy accordingly.

2.Earnings Call Analyzer – run NLP on earnings transcripts to score sentiment and predict post-earnings price direction.

3.Options Greeks Predictor – train models to forecast how delta, gamma, and vega evolve under different market conditions vs. Black-Scholes assumptions.

4.Smart Order Router – build an ML model that decides how to split and time large orders to minimize slippage.

5.Crypto Arbitrage Scanner – detect cross-exchange pricing inefficiencies in real time and model execution feasibility.

6.Factor Risk Model – decompose portfolio returns into explainable risk factors (momentum, value, size) using PCA and regression, then stress test.

7.Volatility Surface Modeler – predict the shape of the implied volatility surface across strikes and expirations using neural nets.

8.Pairs Trading with Cointegration Detection – use ML to dynamically identify co-integrated pairs and automate mean-reversion entries/exits.

9.Reinforcement Learning Market Maker – simulate a market-making agent that learns to set bid-ask spreads and manage inventory risk.

10.Alternative Data Alpha Pipeline – ingest satellite imagery, web traffic, or social sentiment data, engineer features, and backtest a signal.

posts.t: If you’re starting from zero, here’s the correct way to build quant knowledge: 1.
posts.c:
If you’re starting from zero, here’s the correct way to build quant knowledge:

1. Learn how to do quant interview questions 
Quant interviews don’t just test how much math you know, they test how you think under uncertainty. You’re judged on structuring unfamiliar problems, making assumptions, spotting symmetry, and explaining your reasoning live. Past a point, question reps matter more than theory. If you don’t train this explicitly, everything else leaks.

2. Build mathematical intuition, not trivia
You don’t need olympiad maths.
You do need comfort with probability, expectation, conditioning, and optimisation under uncertainty.
Focus on why results hold, not memorising tricks.
If you can explain assumptions, you’re ahead of 90% of candidates.

3. Learn programming as a modelling tool
Python isn’t for syntax points.
It’s for turning ideas into experiments.
Simulate distributions. Stress-test assumptions. Break your own logic.
If your code can’t falsify your thinking, it’s not useful.

4. Study market structure before “strategies”
Most beginners jump straight to alpha ideas.
That’s a mistake.
Understand how markets actually function: liquidity, order flow, transaction costs, latency, constraints.
Strategy without structure is fantasy.

5. Build projects that answer real questions
Not “I implemented X indicator.”
Instead:
“What happens to performance when assumptions fail?”
“What regime does this break in?”
Projects should reveal limits, not hide them.

posts.t: Tired of doing the same Black–Scholes or Monte Carlo projects?
posts.c:
Tired of doing the same Black–Scholes or Monte Carlo projects? Here are 10 quant research ideas you can explore, learn, and replicate to level up your skills

1. Probability of Backtest Overfitting: learn how to detect when your strategies are just curve-fitted to past data.
2. Bayesian Black–Litterman Portfolio Optimization: upgrade classic allocation with Bayesian updates for better uncertainty management.
3. Survival-Based Risk Prediction: use upper and lower partial moments to forecast risk more realistically.
4. Model-Free Reinforcement Learning for Factor Portfolios: let an RL agent optimize your factor exposures without explicit assumptions.
5. Statistics of Sharpe Ratios: understand the reliability and variability of Sharpe ratios across strategies.
6. Systematic Portfolio Trading via Convex Optimization: optimize trades over multiple periods with costs and risk constraints.
7. Time-Series vs Cross-Sectional Factor Analysis: compare carry, momentum, and value strategies across market regimes.
8. Numeraire-Invariant Quadratic Hedging: hedge and optimize portfolios without assuming a risk-free asset.
9. Pricing Exotic Derivatives & Model Risk: value complex options and quantify uncertainty from model assumptions.
10. Regime-Switching Factor Strategies: adapt factor exposures like carry, momentum, and value based on market regimes.
 Pick one, replicate it, and add it to your quant portfolio! 💼

Rick shows Morty how to unlock God Mode—a single folder that gives you instant access to over 200 system settings in one searchable list. If you're serious about performance, you need the master keys. 🚀
Deep Dive Description

"God Mode" (officially known as the Windows Master Control Panel shortcut) is a developer back-door that consolidates every administrative, management, and configuration setting into a single, easy-to-search directory.

How to Unlock It:

 Right-click on your Desktop and select New > Folder.

 Copy and paste this exact string as the name of the folder:

 GodMode.{ED7BA470-8E54-465E-825C-99712043E01C}

 Press Enter.

The folder icon will change to a Control Panel style icon. When you open it, you’ll find everything from advanced disk partitioning and power management to obscure display and security settings. No more jumping through the modern "Settings" app just to find a legacy "Control Panel" feature.

The Takeaway: Efficiency is about reducing the "distance" between you and your tools. The standard Windows UI is designed for the average consumer; God Mode is designed for the architect. By centralizing your controls, you eliminate the cognitive load of navigating menus and get straight to the configuration.

posts.t: Garlic Butter Spaghetti 🔥 Comment “Recipe” and I’ll send you the full recipe card for free!!
posts.c:
Garlic Butter Spaghetti 🔥

Comment “Recipe” and I’ll send you the full recipe card for free!!

Quick, easy, and dangerously good. Buttery garlic heaven with a hint of spice…

Pro Tip: Level it up with chicken, shrimp, or tofu 🫡

Ingredients:

-2 shallots, thinly sliced
-5 garlic cloves, minced
-2 tbsp chili crisp
-1 cup of cream or coconut milk, room temperature
-1 tbsp soy sauce, optional
-1/2 cup fresh Parmesan cheese, grated
-8 oz (225g) pasta of your choice
-2 tbsp butter
-1 tbsp olive oil
-Seasonings (1 tsp each): paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper, oregano

1. Slice your shallots nice and thin and measure out your seasonings. Bring your cream or coconut milk to room temp so it blends in smoothly later.
2. Heat 2 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add the shallots and sauté for 8–10 minutes until soft and starting to turn golden.
3. While the shallots are doing their thing, bring a big pot of salted water to a boil and cook your pasta until al dente. Drain, but save some pasta water… it’s liquid gold. Seriously, don’t you dare dump it. Italians everywhere are watching.
4. Once the shallots are soft and sweet, stir in your minced garlic (fresh garlic only - if you pull out that jarred stuff, the FBI will be at your door in minutes 😅) and all the seasonings. Let them bloom for about a minute, then add the chili crisp and give it another quick sauté.
5. Pour in the cream (or coconut milk), stir in the soy sauce if using, and let it simmer for a few minutes to thicken. Add in the grated Parmesan and stir.
6. Toss your pasta in the sauce until fully coated, adding splashes of reserved pasta water as needed to get that perfect silky consistency.
7. Serve hot with an extra spoonful of chili crisp on top for a little heat and a sprinkle of Parmesan and parsley if you’re feelin’ fancy.

n8n (short for "node 8 node") is a powerful open-source workflow automation tool. It's like a self-hostable alternative to tools like Zapier or Make (formerly Integromat), but with more flexibility and developer-friendly features.

---

🔧 What Can n8n Do?

n8n lets you automate tasks by connecting different apps and services together using visual workflows. Examples:

When you receive an email → extract the data → save it to Google Sheets.

Get a new user in Stripe → send them a welcome email via Gmail → add them to your CRM.

Scrape a website → analyze data with OpenAI → post summary to Slack.

posts.t: This is one of the most beautiful countries in the world.
posts.c:
-follow @thelosttwo for more epic travel inspo✈️

Is 🇵🇼 the most beautiful country in the world?

Welcome to Palau, a place that can only be described as something from another planet 👽🌎

Here, you’ll find towering limestone islands shaped like mushrooms, rising straight out of crystal-clear turquoise waters. These surreal seascapes aren’t just beautiful, they’re protected. In fact, fishing is banned in 80% of the country, making Palau one of the best diving destinations on Earth 🤿🐠🦈

Vibrant coral reefs, manta rays, reef sharks, and sea turtles, the marine life here is everywhere. And with no hotels in its most iconic areas, much of it remains untouched by mass tourism.

If you’re looking for a unique destination to add to your bucketlist, you NEED to put Palau at the very top!

TAG someone that you would bring here 👇🏼

posts.t: En casa nos encantan estos panecillos nube de queso, ajo y oregano, quedan crujientes y esponjosos buenísimos.
posts.c:
Pan nube sin harinas en freidora de aire.
4 ingredientes, keto y ligeros.

Quedan crujientes por fuera y esponjosos por dentro, sin harinas, muy ligeros y sin complicaciones.

Si haces Keto, son perfectos. 

Es una receta que ya la he publicado otras veces con otra versión de sabores, en cuanto a las especias, se le pueden añadir las que más te gusten. 

Ingredientes para 4 bollitos:

3 claras de huevo
100 gr queso rallado, puedes usar el que más te guste
1 cuchara pequeña ajo en polvo
1 cuchara pequeña orégano
Te recomiendo que no les pongas sal, ya que con la del queso es suficiente, pero para gustos colores.

Elaboración:

Bate las claras a punto de nieve.

Añade el queso, las especias y mezcla con movimientos envolventes.

Reparte en 4 bolas en tu freidora de aire y programa 12 min a 180 grados, el tiempo puede variar en función de cada freidora.

En horno serán unos 20 min a 180 grados.

Yo las he hecho en mi @cosori_es TwinFry Dual Blaze, por ser embajadora, tenéis -15% en mis stories destacados, lo que más me gusta de ella es la capacidad, 10L y que tiene 4 resistencias.

Espero que os guste la receta tanto como a mí, gracias por todos vuestros comentarios y qué tengáis un fantástico día.

posts.t: Brown butter Brookies Recipe Ingredients: For the cookie layer: - 1/2 cups unsalted butter, melted
posts.c:
Brown butter Brookies Recipe

Ingredients:

For the cookie layer:

- 1/2 cups unsalted butter, melted and cooled
- 1/2 cup light brown sugar
- 1/3 cup granulated sugar
- 1 large egg, room temp
- 1 tbsp vanilla extract
- 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, spooned and leveled
- 1/2 tsp baking soda
- 1/2 tsp flaky sea salt
- 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips

For the brownie layer:

- 1 cup unsalted butter
- 1/2 cup cocoa powder
- 1 tsp vanilla extract 
- 1/2 cup light brown sugar, spooned and leveled
- 1 3/4 cup powdered sugar
- 3/4 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips
- 1/3 cup semi-sweet chocolate, chopped
- 3 eggs, room temp
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- Pinch of salt
- 3 tbsp olive oil

Method:

1. Preheat oven to 350 F. Line an 8 *8 inch pan with parchment paper.
2. Prepare the cookie layer: Mix flour, baking soda, and salt. Set aside. Combine melted butter, brown and granulated sugar, egg, and vanilla. Whisk until smooth and fluffy for about 2-3 min. Add dry ingredients and chocolate chips. Mix until just combined.

3. Prepare the brownie layer: The browned butter mixture: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir every 10 seconds until foamy (6-8 minutes). Continue until milk solids turn golden brown and smell nutty. Transfer to a heatproof bowl. Add cocoa powder, oil, vanilla, and chopped chocolate; mix until smooth.

In a separate bowl Whisk 3 eggs and light brown sugar for 5-6 minutes until dissolved.
Add powdered sugar; mix 1-2 minutes until combined.Add cooled browned butter mixture; mix until smooth. Add flour and chocolate chips; mix until well combined.

Note: Dissolving sugar in eggs ensures a crackly top.
4.Layer the cookie and brownie batters in the prepared pan.
5. Bake for 40-45 minutes or until the edges are golden and they’re only slightly jiggly from center.( they will set completely once cooled )

6. Let cool completely before cutting into brookies

You can adjust the layering to your preference, either by layering the cookie dough on top of the brownie batter or vice versa
